newsitem.title: USA: Some 70,000 customers still lack power in Mass..
newsitem.headline: Some 70,000 customers still lack power in Mass..

text.p: Some 70,000 utility customers in Massachusetts remained without power on Wednesday and for some power will not be restored until the end of the week, spokesmen for the utility companies said.
The state's largest utility, Massachusetts Electric, a subsidiary of the New England Electric Systems, still had 12,000 customers without power.

"At peak we had 117,000 customers without power. That was yesterday at about 10:30 a.m. Now, we have 12,000 stll out," Massachusetts Electric spokeswoman Jackie Barry said. Some 250 extra crews from Canada, Pennsylvania and New York were brought in to help, she said.
"We hope to have the majority of those 12,000 restored by the end of the day, but there are some places we just can't physically get to and those will take a little longer," Barry said.
Commonwealth Electric, a subsidiary of Commonwealth Energy Systems, reported that two of its three transmission lines to Cape Cod and Martha's Vineyard were still down.
"We have one transmission line that is still operating and we hope to have the other two lines back today," Commonwealth Electric spokesman Peter Dimond said.

Some 29,100 customers were affected by the outtage - 20,000 of them on Cape Cod. The resort island of Martha's Vineyard was completely without power Wednesday morning and Dimond said power to all customers would not be fully restored until the end of the week.
Some 45 crews from as far away as Maryland, Maine and Canada were helping the utility's own 70 crews restore power "and we have calls out to other utilities for help," Dimond said

In Boston, Boston Edison was still trying to restore power to its customers. A spokesman could not be immediately reached for details, but radio reports estimated some 40,000 customers remained without power.
The two-day blizzard of '97 dumped up to three feet of snow on New England bringing parts of the region to a complete halt.
A state of emergency remains in effect for Massachusetts and most schools are closed. The state National Guard is helping municipalities to clear roads of the thousands of downed trees.
Winds in the eastern part of the state remained quite strong Wednesday morning. Wind gusts of 57 mph were recorded Wednesday morning at Nantucket off the coast of Cape Cod.

Officials at the state's emergency management agency were preparing for the possibility of flooding Wednesday as waves up to 20 feet high continued to pound the coast and the snow slowly melts in already saturated in-land areas.
